text: Descartes's doctrine of continuous creation — that God must re-create (conserve) the world at every moment — rests on which key premise?
choices: Time is merely the order of succession among events, not a container
Every genuine idea must be a copy of a prior sensory or introspective impression
The parts of time are ontologically independent, so a thing's existing at one moment does not entail its existing at the next
Simultaneity is relative to an observer's inertial frame of reference
explanation: Continuous creation follows from the ontological independence of temporal moments: because a thing's existing at one instant does not by itself guarantee its existing at the next, God's ongoing creative act is required for the world to persist (Third Meditation; Principles I.21). Choice 0 is Leibniz's relationalism and choice 1 is Hume's copy principle, both from other thinkers; choice 3 is a twentieth-century relativistic idea entirely foreign to Descartes.
